what_happened: On 2026-11-06 the person running Athena lifted, by hand and outside any job, the scope-guard pause on the stale-job retry line so the batch could retry it. The earlier attempt's code had passed its checks. It was rejected because of a criterion the reader added, which the append-only decision log cannot satisfy, plus some wording fixes. Athena's proposed retry already drops that criterion. The pause would have blocked the retry. Lifting it lets the retry resume the kept candidate and avoids repeating the spend. No acceptance criteria, findings or checks are listed for this event.
cause: The scope guard counts spend per line and does not ask why an attempt did not land. Spend on an attempt whose code passed all checks, but which was rejected for an unmeetable reader-added criterion or for wording, looks the same as progress-less spend. The guard cannot tell a retry that changes the cause (the criterion is dropped) from a repeat of the same failure. It also cannot see that a kept candidate exists, so a resume costs little. Nothing in the pause records its reason or says when it should lift. Because the guard has no rule for 'checks passed, only the criterion or wording was wrong', a person must read the outcome and lift the pause. The same gap appeared earlier today with a stale base.
prevention: Make the scope guard classify each attempt's stop reason before it counts spend. Spend should not count toward the pause when the attempt passed all code checks and was stopped for something other than a code defect. Examples are a stale base, an environment stop, or a rejection caused only by an unmeetable or reader-added criterion or by wording. When a kept candidate exists and the next retry's reading differs from the rejected one, as when a criterion is dropped, the guard should apply no pause and should show the expected cost of a resume. A pause that does apply should record its reason and the condition that lifts it.
proposed_request: Change the scope guard so that spend from an attempt does not count toward pausing a line when the attempt passed all code checks and ended for a non-code reason: a stale base, an environment stop, or a rejection caused only by a reader-added criterion that cannot be met or by wording fixes. Outcome: such lines are not paused, and a retry resumes the kept candidate. Acceptance: (1) a test replays the 2026-11-06 stale-job retry line and the 2026-11-06 build-slot line and shows neither is paused; (2) a line whose attempts failed code checks still pauses at the existing threshold; (3) when the guard does pause a line, it records the stop reason and the lifting condition in the pause record, and the pause is shown by the status command; (4) the retry output shows whether it will resume a kept candidate or rebuild. No manual pause lift is needed in either replayed case.
